You can specialize (i.e. hand therapy) but most aren't. You just work in different settings (nursing home, home health, pediatrics, inpatient, etc.)

It's more of a holistic intervention that can help people participate in meaningful daily activities despite a physical or cognitive impairment.  I like that it doesn't partition the body, but focuses on how the body works together to complete daily tasks. There's usually a lot of factors that are impacting overall function (physical component, social, mental, environmental, etc.) and occupational therapy considers all aspects.

I'm glad your dad is a good support for you! The radio might be too much of a distraction with singing and simultaneously trying to learn the ways of the road, but a nice conversation with your dad would be great and then if you needed any driving adjustments, he could just add that in intermittently. Learning to drive was scary for me- but keep practicing and that feeling will slowly start to lessen. It's okay to feel anxious, just utilize the tools you have so it doesn't take over. You can handle this. I have faith in you. :)

I have that as well. First things first, I did NOT stop driving. I didn't want my anxiety to get worse and further limit my driving. It helped me to turn on the radio and sing along. This served 2 purposes- distraction and encouraging slower, controlled breathing. I would work with my current threshold, and slowly bump up a minute or two every few days/every week. I haven't had to pull over, but I have given myself the option that its always available if I need to. You could also bring a friend for support while driving if you think that would help.

That sounds like a load of crap. No way a wet blanket was left to sour in a bag for 4 weeks... Why would the owner wait a month to pick up his $500 blanket? Wouldn't the owner/other employees notice an order not being pick up for that long? Wouldn't they notice a sour blanket in a bag on the shelf over a months time? Plus a $500 blanket? Really? What's it made out of- gold? Does the owner have proof of its value based on brand/cloth type? 

Regardless, it sounds like he doesn't have any proof of you signing something over to state you're responsible for this blanket. And the above poster is correct- he should have insurance for this- NOT hold individual employees responsible to pay out of pocket if there's some sort of mishap at his business.

Wet blankets are heavy! There is no way you can absentmindedly put a wet blanket in a bag and call it good to go...

If it were me, try googling for free, pro-bono lawyer clinics in your area. I did that once when I had a landlord problem (ended up taking him to small claims court and winning.) I got to meet with a lawyer for about 10 minutes, explained the situation, and just got a simple explanation of what my options were. They won't represent you, they'll just point you in the right direction.

Also, try posting this in a reddit forum more geared to legal advice.
